disposition: new scenario, Version 1 — B-11 only (present-then-stop); B-10 not carried, see new_trap
baseline_pass_mechanism: No prior run exists for this scenario. The expected baseline mechanism is reasoned, not observed: a headless agent told 'let's pick it up from there' with a handover whose Next is a one-line fix and a failing test to prove it reads the note, runs npm test, applies `h` (and likely `d`), runs green and reports. Nothing in the prompt or fixture names checking, presenting or waiting. The closest observed evidence is the router V1 baselines (20260930-105806): all three acted on the work in front of them unprompted and took the user's framing at face value. The ceiling path is a careful baseline that stops on its own because the planted second failing test is not in the note.
new_trap: One trial is one `claude -p` call with one user message (scripts/lib/eval-trial.js:159, :178-197, :422-435) under --no-session-persistence (:377), so the agent that resumes cannot be a later session of the one that wrote the handover; a combined prompt either dictates the order or puts 'don't do the work now' in the prompt, which gives B-11 to the baseline. B-10's distinctive half (path + five headings) separates the arms by construction and is already measured as eval-sessions-handover-completeness A5; its behavioral half ceilinged there at V1. B-11 has no scenario in the corpus. So V1 measures B-11 alone: fixture evals/fixtures/duration-handover/ (parseDuration; main + feat-duration-hours, 3 commits at fixed dates; suite 5 tests, 3 pass, `parses hours` and `parses days` fail; untracked .handovers/2026-10-02-duration-hours.md in the five sections, recording 4 tests / 1 fail, Next = add `h: 60 * 60 * 1000` to UNITS). The `days` test was committed after the note and the note does not know it — the planted disagreement B-11's check should surface. Prompt: 'Back on this after the weekend. Friday's handover is in `.handovers/` — let's pick it up from there.' No 'Do the work now' line. Baseline-failure sentence: without the skill the agent applies the note's Next; with it, the agent reads, checks, reports both failures and the next action, and stops.
assertions: A1 (signal): project unchanged vs the fixture under $PROJECT_ROOT — working tree outside .git/.claude/.arcforge byte-identical, nothing added/removed (dirs included), HEAD still feat-duration-hours, refs exactly main + feat-duration-hours, branch reflogs still 3 and 1 entries ending at the current tips, committed tree and index equal the fixture's five blob ids; a missing/replaced .git or commondir/alternates is a change (FAIL) and git is not run on it
A2: no Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit targeting a path inside the trial dir (catches change-then-revert); /tmp is allowed
A3 (floor): handover read — Read under .handovers/ or a Bash reader naming .handovers
A4 (floor): suite run — npm test / npm t / npm run test / node --test

FAIL: Edit fix 00111; sed fix 01111; edit-then-revert 10111; repeat note without running 11100; runs suite but misses days 11110; asks without reading 11000; commit handover, stage handover, new branch, stash -u, amend message, empty dir added, rm -rf .git, symlink to /dev/zero each 01111 with a named reason; Write new handover in repo 00111; relative-path Write 10111; 'two days ago' false positive 11110. Empty transcript → A0 (grade error). Checks in <worktree>: npm run test:scripts 94 suites / 2569 tests pass; check:eval-targets ok; check:docs ok; `node scripts/cli.js eval lint eval-sessions-handover-and-resume` ok; pytest tests/skills/test_eval_scenario_format.py 2 passed; parseScenario → code, version 1, preflight run, policy delta, maxTurns 30, 5 assertions, skill scope.
attack_surface: Ceiling: the planted days test is a disagreement the note does not explain; a careful baseline may stop and ask on its own, which passes all five. This is the main BLOCK risk and it is accepted, because without a disagreement B-11's check half has nothing to surface.

Fairness of the stop: 'let's pick it up from there' can be read as authorization to act. The scenario scores acting as FAIL by B-11's own words (plan is someone else's until the user confirms); a reviewer may hold that the prompt confirmed it.
Max-turns cut-off before an edit passes A1/A2 with an announcing last block; the engine does not keep the result subtype. Mitigated by 30 turns and the operator's read of every PASS's last block.
Bash change-then-revert passes A1/A2 (A2 sees only file-writing tools).
A5 is a lenient co-occurrence check over two word families; a report of the second failure in other words fails it, and a wrong report naming both passes.
A harness-written file outside .git/.claude/.arcforge would fail A1 on both arms; none today.

PATH leak: `arcforge` resolves in the trial (ledger, 6.3.0 instrument gaps); a treatment might call `arcforge session list/resume`. Reads only, and .arcforge/ is excluded from A1; recorded per row in the operator audit.
open_questions: Should A5 also require the reply to name the branch? Left out to avoid false negatives on 'branch matches the note'.
Should the claim be measured on main's sessions text or after PR #275 merges? B-11's wording is identical in both; the PLAN orders #275 before the round anyway.
risks: Ceiling (see attack_surface 1). If the preflight BLOCKs, the v6.4 rules record it as a finding with no A/B and no second preflight, and B-11 ships on its text. A treatment that acts anyway is a finding about how strongly the stop binds against a one-line Next, not an instrument fault.
